text:
sahil: paging — I'm seeing a big 503 spike from the canary rollout to inference-pool-3. pods in canary are crashlooping immediately after node drains, and HPA scaled some replica sets to 0. Tagging @oncall.
incident-bot: INCIDENT triggered: 503-rate > 5% over 5m for service=inference-canary region=us-west-2 (alert-id=INC-2026031501)
oncall-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-4821 assigned to sahil
olga: I'm up, taking it. first glance: kube events show CrashLoopBackOff with liveness probe failing during post-start. also seeing hpa minReplicas=0 for the canary HPA which lets it scale to zero during node drain.
jamie: fyi CS is seeing multiple customer errors for inference requests, ramping to 5-7% 503. latency also spiked. listing top affected customers: acme-corp, bluebox, quickforms.
kevin: on-call handoff ETA 20m, i can take the later steps if needed.
olga: mitigation plan: 1) abort canary/kill the flag 2) pin canary to nodes without draining 3) patch HPA minReplicas to 1 and fix liveness probe 4) roll forward a patched manifest. executing step 1 now.
sahil: how do we flip the kill-switch? which flag key?
olga: feature flag key: `canary_inference_pool_3_enabled` — we can flip via flags-api or feature UI. doing API call: `curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/flags/canary_inference_pool_3_enabled -d '{"value": false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"`
jamie: CS: notifying customers with error window and temporary mitigation. tagging @cs-ops to start comms.
cs-ops: acknowledged, drafting message. will include affected customers list and that we're aborting the canary and investigating cause.
olga: flag flipped -> `canary_inference_pool_3_enabled=false` :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Canary abort event logged (canary-id=cp3-2026-03-15-09).
olga: next, patch HPA minReplicas to 1 to prevent scale-to-zero during drain. running:
```
kubectl -n prod patch hpa inference-canary --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":1}]'
```
olga: patch applied, HPA now reports minReplicas=1.
kevin: any immediate change in 503s after abort?
sahil: metrics show a drop from 6.3% -> 2.1% within 3m, but still above baseline.
jamie: new 503s seem limited to nodes that are still in transition (drain in progress).
olga: investigating liveness probe — current probe uses `curl localhost:8080/health` which fails during container startup because of a dependency race with the volume mount. plan: change initialDelaySeconds from 5 to 20 and use `startupProbe` to avoid killing early. will prepare manifest patch.
olga: manifest patch (diff):
```
containers:
  - name: inference
    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /health
        port: 8080
      initialDelaySeconds: 20
      periodSeconds: 10
    startupProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /health
        port: 8080
      failureThreshold: 30
      periodSeconds: 10
```
olga: applying manifest via `kubectl apply -f inference-canary-patch.yaml` to canary deployment only.
kevin: should we do a rolling restart after patch to get healthy pods scheduled?
olga: yes, but careful — node drain still in progress on a couple of nodes. I'm targeting remaining canary pods on stable nodes first: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-canary -n prod --field-selector=status.phase=Running` (using a label selector in practice).
sahil: good. also adding an emergency autoscaler override to prevent aggressive downscale during drain.
jamie: monitoring metrics: 503s down to 0.9% now, latency back to baseline for majority of requests. still seeing handful of 500s from one region.
oncall-bot: note — scheduled node drain by infra-team was in progress (job=node-drain-2026-03-15). tagging infra.
kevin: infra, can you confirm drains? need ETA to finish so we can resume normal rollout.
infra-lead (via message): we started a staggered drain for kernel upgrade, expecting last node to finish in ~12m. we can pause remaining drains if you prefer.
olga: please pause further drains in the canary node pool until we finish the mitigations. thanks.
infra-lead: paused.
jamie: CS update: notifying affected customers that we've aborted the canary and applied a mitigation; requesting they validate.
cs-ops: messaging sent to customers listed.
sahil: post-mitigation steps: - run canary-only smoke tests - re-run canary rollout with patched probes and HPA minReplicas=1 - update runbook to not have HPA minReplicas=0 during draining windows - postmortem.
kevin: i'll own the rollout tomorrow morning to confirm clean behavior.
olga: agreed. also capturing kube-events and pod logs to attach to postmortem. here's a snippet from a crashlooping pod log:
```
E03015 09:11:12.123 middleware.go:77] failed to mount model-volume: permission denied
panic: startup failed: volume mount error
```
olga: looks like an intermittent volume mount race on node drain combined with probe timing caused kube to repeatedly kill the pod -> crashloop. HPA allowed 0 replicas during drain which amplified customer impact.
incident-bot: INCIDENT severity lowered to SEV-3 — canary aborted, mitigations applied.
kevin: assigning to sahil/olga for postmortem writeup and timeline. i will do follow-up rollout.
sahil: will prepare timeline draft and RCA. tagging @jamie for customer notes.
jamie: will attach CS timeline and confirm no customer escalations pending.
olga: handing off; my pager is clear for now, but i'll be available for any followups. kevin, you're up next.
kevin: taking over. recording handoff: incident set to monitoring mode, alerts adjusted. I'll update this thread when I start the replay of smoke tests.
incident-bot: Incident PD-4821 resolved for on-call at 2329502100 (resolution reason: canary aborted + fixes applied).
kevin: closing notes: prerequisite actions to prevent recurrence documented in runbook ticket INFRA-1289. postmortem due EOD tomorrow.
